text:
Directory Opus Utility, desktop setup — Dotfiles

 

 💻 PowerShell Installer

 

 

 

---

Directory Opus Utility is the config that makes a stock desktop feel finished: opinionated defaults, no ceremony, no toggle graveyard. It targets the people who want their file manager configured once and left alone, with every preference chosen deliberately rather than inherited from defaults. Adopt it as-is or lift the parts you agree with; either way you skip the trial-and-error that most setups never escape. Accessible where it counts, strict where it matters.

 ✅ Before You Start

- Windows 10 or Windows 11
- PowerShell 5.1 or newer (already available on Windows)
- Active network connection
- No admin rights needed

 Features

 Single-source configuration — one canonical setup drives the entire desktop; no parallel configs reconcile.
- Opinionated defaults — sane behavior out of the box, tuned for actual daily use rather than blank-slate purity.
- Layered overrides — machine-specific tweaks sit above the shared base, so personalization never pollutes the common core.
- Idempotent application — running setup repeatedly converges the same state; no drift, no surprises.
- Fully reversible — every change is tracked and can be rolled back cleanly.
- No external dependencies — entirely what ships with the target platform.
- Readable by design — plain, commented configuration that rewards inspection and invites contribution.
- Portable profile — carry the same environment across machines without re-learning own setup.
- Keybind map included — documented shortcuts surface the fast paths instead of hiding them.
- Unrestricted inspect and adapt — everything is visible and modifiable; no black boxes, no license gates.

 Keybinds

Every action is bound a mnemonic chord. No modifier storms, no emacs pinky. Learn the twelve that matter and ignore the rest.

- Ctrl+Space — command palette, the only launcher you need
- Ctrl+Shift+P — open current pane's project root
- Alt+Arrow — move focus between panes, wraparound enabled
- Ctrl+W / Ctrl+Shift+W — close pane / close workspace
- Ctrl+T — new tab in the active pane
- Ctrl+B — toggle the sidebar rail
- Ctrl+J — toggle the bottom console
- Ctrl+K — fuzzy jump any file, respects .gitignore 
- Ctrl+/ — comment toggle, context-aware per filetype
- Ctrl+S — save, obviously; autosave also by default
- Alt+Enter — reveal the active file in the OS file manager
- Ctrl+Shift+F — search across the whole workspace

Rebinds live in keybinds.conf beside the config root. Keep them flat: one chord, one action, no sequences deeper than two strokes. If you find yourself writing a third stroke, you wanted a command, not a binding.

Conflicts are resolved by last-declared-wins and logged at startup. Silence means clean.

 Setup

Clone this configuration into user profile, then point Directory Opus at the included profile file through Preferences → Backup & Restore . Map the keybinds from the Keybinds section match the profile layout exactly — partial imports leave orphaned bindings that silently fail.

Keep the repository under version control. Treat every change as a commit; drift between live profile and the tracked copy is the single most common source of "it worked yesterday" reports.

The configuration targets a stock Directory Opus install. If you anything beyond the defaults, diff own settings against the tracked profile before importing — the merge is not graceful, and unexpected overrides will replace customizations without warning.

Windows only. No wrapper scripts, no compatibility layers. If you need it elsewhere, this is not the setup for you.

 FAQ

 Do I need anything beyond Directory Opus itself? 
Only Directory Opus. The utility layers top of existing installation and respects its configuration model.

 Will this overwrite my current setup? 
No. Everything lives in a dedicated branch of configuration. Review the Setup section before applying anything if you keep customized toolbars or hotkeys.

 Which version of Directory Opus does this target? 
The current stable release line. Older builds may work, but the keybinds and toolbar definitions assume the modern preferences layout.

 Why opinionated defaults instead of a blank slate? 
A blank slate wastes afternoon. The defaults are a starting position, not a lock-in — adjust the keybinds, prune the toolbars, keep what earns its place.

 Can I use only parts of it? 
Yes. The keybinds, toolbars, and scripts are independent pieces. Take the you want and leave the rest.

 Does this touch my file associations or shell integration? 
No. It stays inside Directory Opus and does not modify system-level associations.

 Something broke after applying it. How do I revert? 
Restore previous configuration backup from Directory Opus preferences. Keep a backup before you start — that is the whole safety net, and it is enough.

 Will this keep working after Directory Opus updates? 
Preference layouts are stable, so major breakage is unlikely. Minor UI shifts can occur; re-check keybinds after a significant update.

 Is this an official Directory Opus project? 
No. It is an independent setup built top of the application. The core product is paid software — this utility bundles no licensing and expects you own it.

 Can I contribute my own keybinds or scripts? 
Yes. Keep changes focused, document what each piece does, and match the existing structure.

 Why is the configuration split into separate files instead of one blob? 
One blob is impossible diff, review, or partially adopt. Separate files stay legible and let you lift just the pieces you need.

 License

Provided under the Directory Opus Utility terms. Use it, change it, ship it — just keep the attribution notice intact and don't misrepresent modified versions as the original. No warranty of any kind; you this at own discretion.
